## Scoring guide 

### Content

- Getting the right answer is only a small part of the grade
- Good quality interpretation of your results is the name of the game
- If you see something that looks unusual in your data (outlier, some unusual distribution type) - investigate it! 
- When explaining your results, say something interesting about them. Did it match your expectations? Why or why not? 
- Brief explanations that simply repeat what I can visually see myself will not receive a good score
- On the other hand, filling the homework with paragraphs of not very interesting description is not valuable either. The goal isn't to write the most words, but find the most interesting things in the data.
- You do not need to be an expert in pollution or AQI to get a good grade on this assignment, but I will expect you to look up basic information, such as what does `shortwave_radiation_sum_mj_m2` mean and so on to help you understand and set expectations your data.
- The information requested in the question prompts are only a starting point, if you find other interesting information along the way, please report that. You don't need to look at the data forever but if there is obviously something else interesting in the data you should report it.
- You must have up to Question 2 completed for the homework preliminary check on Sunday, September 13

### Technical

- Make sure your graphs are produced using `ggplot()`, are well labeled, and are easy to read. Using `ggplot()` is a requirement.
- Make sure your tables are produced with the `kable()` function from the `knitr` package, are well labeled, and are easy to read. You can make your tables prettier with the `kableExtra` package. Using `kable()` is a requirement.
- Regression tables should be made in an appealing, easy to read format. Using `modelsummary()` is a requirement.
- Make sure you do not have anything rendered in your HTML file besides your results and, when asked for by a question, your code. That means no warnings, messages, or other unnecessary output should appear in your final rendered HTML file.

# Air pollution

One interesting issue for anyone living in the greater Shanghai area is thinking about which days are likely to have the highest unhealthy air days. While the air in Shgnahi is much cleaner than it was in previous decades, there are still a number of days per year that the air is unhealthy. One obvious factor that influences the air pollution levels is the weather. This assignment asks you to consider the relationship between unhealthy air pollution and the weather. The dataset is a subset of data taken from [here](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/houjihao/china-capitals-weather-and-air-quality-2023-2026/data), credit to user `houjihao`.

### 5b. Interpreting coefficients of 5a. model

Carefully interpret your coefficients from 5a. What do they mean? How do we know if the slopes are large or small? 

### 5c. Add `season`

For this question, you will need to use the `mutate()` and `case_when()` verbs to create a new variable called `season`. You will also need the library `lubridate()` (information about this library is [here](https://www.epirhandbook.com/en/new_pages/dates.html)) It should have the values of `spring`, `summer`, `fall`, and `winter`. Interpret your coefficients and compare them to 5b. What do they mean? If there are any significant changes to the coefficients, why do you think they changed?

### 5d. Thinking about your results

Consider the results of 5a.-5c. together. What can we learn about what determines air pollution? How did your conclusions change from Q3 and Q4? Why do you think they changed? Do these results overall match your original expectations?

## 6. In summary (20 points)

Sum up everything that you have learned from questions 1-5. Do not simply repeat/rephrase your previous results but try to say something larger that synthesizes the results together to draw a more meaningful general conclusion. 

- Compare your expectations from Q1 to your results throughout your investigations. Explain how your investigations changed your conclusions as you explored the data more deeply. 
- What can we conclude about the relationship between the weather and air pollution? What are some issues that this data cannot answer that need more investigation?
